title: I Heard the Voice of Jesus Say
description: I Heard the Voice of Jesus Say in Tonic Solfa to MATERNA, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Horatius Bonar wrote these words. They were printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 46.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre Double (8.6.8.6.8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MATERNA; any other Common Metre Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: I heard the voice of Je-sus say, “Come un-to Me and rest; Lay down, thou wea-ry one, lay down Thy head up-on My breast!” I came to Je-sus as I was, Wea-ry and worn and sad; I found in Him a rest-ing place, And He has made me glad.

lines: I heard the voice of Jesus say,
“Come unto Me and rest;
Lay down, thou weary one, lay down
Thy head upon My breast!”
I came to Jesus as I was,
Weary and worn and sad;
I found in Him a resting-place,
And He has made me glad.
I heard the voice of Jesus say,
“Behold, I freely give
The living water; thirsty one,
Stoop down and drink and live!”
I came to Jesus, and I drank
Of that life-giving stream;
My thirst was quenched, my soul revived,
And now I live in Him.
I heard the voice of Jesus say,
“I am this dark world’s Light;
Look unto Me, thy morn shall rise
And all thy day be bright!”
I looked to Jesus, and I found
In Him my Star, my Sun;
And in that Light of Life I’ll walk
Till traveling days are done.

licence: Public domain: Horatius Bonar died in 1889.
credits: Words by Horatius Bonar (1808–1889), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to MATERNA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
